title: Batching scheduler oscillation and KV-cache incoherence investigation
summary: On 2026-02-17 we observed intermittent tail-latency spikes for a subset of Hosted API and Dedicated customers. Root cause traces back to scheduler oscillation interacting with KV cache invalidation logic, producing a cyclical load pattern and repeated cold-KV fetches. A targeted hotfix to the scheduler backoff policy and a KV-cache gating change was validated in canary and rolled out to mitigate the SLO misses.
impact: Between 2026-02-17 04:20 UTC and 2026-02-17 11:05 UTC ~2.1% of requests to gen endpoints experienced p99 > 900ms (baseline p99 ~ 150-220ms). Two enterprise Dedicated customers reported increased latency and one customer escalated to SEs claiming production degradation. No model correctness/regression or data loss observed. Cost increased ~12% on affected pools due to redundant cache repopulation.
timeline:
2026-02-17 04:12 UTC: First alert (p99 spike) on cluster-r1.
2026-02-17 04:20 UTC: SEs notified; initial mitigation: redirect traffic to warm pools.
2026-02-17 05:05 UTC: Profiling capture (perf+trace) started on affected nodes.
2026-02-17 06:30 UTC: Observed scheduler flush/backoff pattern correlating with KV cache miss storms.
2026-02-17 08:00 UTC: Hypothesis formed: scheduler oscillation timers + aggressive KV invalidation on spike -> cold fetch thrash.
2026-02-17 09:15 UTC: Canary hotfix deployed (scheduler backoff + kv gating).
2026-02-17 10:00 UTC: Canary metrics show p99 return to baseline.
2026-02-17 11:05 UTC: Hotfix rolled to 60% of affected capacity. Continued monitoring.
2026-02-18 14:00 UTC: Full rollout complete after validation.
detailed_findings:
1) Profiling: CPU and GPU HPL traces show periodic bursts of short-lived worker processes that caused repeated KV cache evictions. Flamegraphs indicate spikes in kernel scheduling and memcpy around the same intervals as network reads for KV population.
2) Scheduler behavior: The continuous-batching scheduler uses a dynamic time-window that shrinks under perceived congestion; under a burst pattern it collapsed windows quickly which dropped queued requests and caused immediate retries. Retries bypassed soft-prefix-KV check because of timing, generating extra cache repopulation requests.
3) KV cache logic: We found a race when the cache invalidation timer coexists with a forced refresh path. When the scheduler restarted a batch, the path to validate cached KV entries was sometimes skipped, triggering cold fetch.
4) Amplifier: A small proportion of requests had long input prefixes (avg +1.8x KV items) which increased fetch cost and made the oscillation visible at p99 even though p50 stayed stable.
5) Metrics correlation: The request-retry-ratio metric (new) rose from 0.6% to 6.8% during incident windows, matching p99 spikes.
root_cause: Interplay of scheduler backoff heuristics (over-aggressive shrink on transient congestion) and a KV-cache validation race condition. The scheduler's aggressive shrink led to more retries that hit a codepath not performing prefix-aware KV checks, causing repeated cold-KV loads and amplification of tail latency.
mitigation_and_hotfixes:
Short-term (emergency): 1) Route critical customer traffic to warm pools and reserve capacity for affected clusters. 2) Increase scheduler minimum window to avoid shrink oscillation. 3) Temporarily disable the forced-refresh path on KV cache.
Hotfix PR: #2391 (scheduler: introduce exponential backoff floor; kvcache: add validation gating). Deployed to canary 2026-02-17 09:15 UTC, monitored for one hour, then progressive rollout. Hotfix validated by latency and retry metrics returning to baseline.
Observability changes in hotfix: emit explicit 'kvcache.validation_skipped' and 'scheduler.shrink_event' counters for future diagnosis.
validation:
Canary validation windows: 2026-02-17 09:15-10:15 UTC. Observed p99 reduced from ~950ms to ~210ms in canary nodes; request-retry-ratio dropped from 6.5% to 0.9%; KV fetch QPS decreased by ~72% on canary. Load testing: synthetic replay of the spike pattern (using src/tools/replay) showed no oscillation with the patched scheduler on same machine configs.
Test matrix: microbench (unit) + integration (canary) + synthetic stress replay; all green. Post-rollout checks: 1, 4, and 24-hour p99 reports show stable baselines.
customer_communication: Drafted message for affected customers: apology, explanation (non-technical summary) and mitigation steps taken, plus offer for credits for SLA breach. SEs already contacted two dedicated customers with a technical write-up and timeline. Customer feedback: one customer wanted detailed postmortem (provided), another requested follow-up audit of Dedicated pool configurations.
longer_term_actions:
1) Scheduler rework: Evaluate a hybrid shrink strategy that considers KV-load signals before shrinking. (owner: Arjun Patel, ETA Q2 2026)
2) KV-cache hardening: eliminate validation races and add stronger invariants around forced refresh path. (owner: Ivy Zhang, ETA Q2 2026)
3) Introduce 'retry amplification' alert (when retry-ratio climbs >2% of baseline). (owner: Sofia Martinez, ETA 2026-03-05)
4) Add end-to-end synthetic traffic generator for prefix-heavy workloads to CI to catch this pattern. (owner: Liam O'Connor, ETA 2026-04-01)
5) Dedicated customer audit: offer configuration review and recommended warm pool policies. (owner: Maya Chen, ETA 2026-03-01)

lessons_learned:
- Systemic failures often arise from interactions between heuristics (scheduler) and edge codepaths (cache refresh). Single-component perf improvements can regress when they change signal timing.
- Observability gaps: missing explicit counters made correlation slower; we should instrument state transitions where race gaps exist.
- Canary + synthetic stress replay were effective in preventing rollback; make replay harness part of standard incident runbook.
notes_to_self: Follow up with infra on whether autoscaler noise could have exacerbated the shrink signals. Re-run experiments with synthetic tail-heavy payloads across VM types (A100 vs H100) to confirm no hardware-specific effects.
conclusion: Root cause was not a single bug but a timing-dependent interaction between scheduler heuristics and cache validation. The applied hotfix is validated, restored SLOs, and reduced unnecessary KV traffic. Longer-term changes are planned to remove fragility.
